channel.title: Banks & NBFCs · Market Pressure Map
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Banks & NBFCs in Indian markets. Today: tailwind (+2.0).

item.title: [+2] Foreign investors bought a net ₹84,291 crore of Indian equities from 2 to 13 November, depository data show
item.description:
That is about $8.9 billion over nine sessions, after October's ₹34,843 crore outflow; debt inflows included ₹7,815 crore via the fully accessible route. 2026 is still a net outflow of about ₹2.56 lakh crore. Ongoing, up from ₹53,739 crore a week ago.

Banks & NBFCs: tailwind (+2) — Main destination for foreign money

Why it matters: Inflows on this scale underpin equities and the rupee and help fund the wider goods deficit, but can slow as US yields rise.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +3, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Rupee +1, Bond market (G-Secs) +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: [+1] Sensex opens about 0.5% higher near 82,033 and Nifty near 25,240 as crude eases; rupee at 94.22
item.description:
Indices recovered Friday's losses in early Monday trade, though realty and metal indices fell about 1%. The rupee opened 3 paise firmer. Wholesale inflation data is due today. Reversing Friday's 0.61% Nifty fall.

Banks & NBFCs: mild tailwind (+1) — Index heavyweights lead

Why it matters: Softer oil and continued foreign buying are offsetting rate-hike worries; weak metals reflect poor Chinese data, and the wholesale inflation print is the next test.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: [−1] US 10-year yield holds at 5.14% with a December Fed hike fully priced; gold near $3,890 after 4.6% weekly fall
item.description:
The dollar index was steady at 103.42, its highest since April last year; the 2-year yield is 4.87% after a 35 bps weekly jump. The Fed chair speaks today. Ongoing from Friday.

Banks & NBFCs: mild headwind (−1) — Global funding costs

Why it matters: High US yields and a strong dollar keep pressure on the rupee and G-Sec yields and could slow foreign inflows; cheaper gold trims India's import bill.

Market gauges: Rupee −1, Bond market (G-Secs) −1, Foreign investor flows −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks
